counterargs.read: The tension today is between rates and vol: nominal and (implied) real yields rise with the dollar after a soft 2Y auction, yet MOVE eases below 80 and credit spreads tighten. That combination reads as orderly front-end repricing -- duration repricing, not intermediation stress -- rather than a funding or liquidity problem. But the 2Y's thin indirect demand is the second soft mix in three auctions, so the 5Y today and 7Y tomorrow matter: another weak indirect/heavy dealer print in the same Note bucket would satisfy the two-auction confirmation rule for an Early Warning downgrade. Until then, the regime read stays Controlled Tightening with a Stable short-term tone.
